faq.q: Which way does the Earth spin?
faq.a: From west to east. Seen from far above the North Pole, it turns anticlockwise. That is why places further east see sunrise before places further west.

faq.q: Why do the stars move across the sky?
faq.a: They don't really move; we do. As the Earth spins eastwards, the whole sky seems to turn the other way, so stars rise in the east and set in the west, just like the Sun.

faq.q: Does the Sun always rise exactly in the east?
faq.a: No. It rises due east only around the equinoxes in March and September. In northern summer it rises in the north-east, and in northern winter in the south-east.
asks: Where does the Sun rise in summer?

faq.q: Does the Sun rise in the east on every planet?
faq.a: No. Venus spins backwards, so there the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east, very slowly, because one Venus day lasts about 117 Earth days.
asks: Is there a planet where the Sun rises in the west?

faq.q: Why does Japan see sunrise before Britain?
faq.a: Japan lies far to the east, so the Earth's eastward spin carries it into sunlight hours before Britain. That is one reason Japan is called the land of the rising sun.
asks: Why is Japan called the land of the rising sun?

facts: Seen from above the North Pole, Earth rotates anticlockwise, from west to east.
The Sun rises due east and sets due west only around the March and September equinoxes.
On Venus, which spins backwards, the Sun rises in the west.
